newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end higher after Band B cellular bids.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end higher after Band B cellular bids.

text.p: Brazil stocks closed higher on continuing optimism about the privatisation of the telecommunications sector after the government received bids from groups interested in the Band B cellular concessions, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most liquid shares ended up 1.35 percent at 9,837 points. Market turnover totalled 698.8 million reais ($660.4 million reais).
The Brazilian government on Monday received bids from 15 consortia comprising foreign and local investors for nine of its 10 cellular concession areas.
The sale of the Band B cellular services, which is expected to generate between five to six billion reais, is the first step in the much-awaited privatization of the country's telecom industry.
Analysts also said the market continued to reflect last week's telecom rate restructuring, which is expected to have a positive impact on the results of Telebras and its subsidiaries.
Telebras preferred rose 1.23 percent, closing at 123.50 reais, while its common stock gained 1.79 percent.
Power shares also helped drive the Bovespa index higher, traders said.
Traders now speculate the government will raise electricity rates after the telephone rate rebalancing. jumped 4.43 percent to close at 495 reais.
Minas Gerais state power firm Cemig gained 3.43 percent to 48.20 reais, while Cesp soared 7.39 percent, closing at 59.60 reais.
The power sector index, comprising the nine most liquid stocks in the electrical sector, ended up 3.89 percent at 2,718 points.

Brazilian bolsas changed their trading hours today. The stock exchanges are now opening at 1000 local/1300 GMT and closing at 1700 local/2000 GMT, with one-hour break at lunch time. Trading remains non-stop electronically.
